flake-floors.title: Flake Epoxy Floors
flake-floors.meta_description: Full-broadcast flake epoxy floors installed in one day across Portland. Slip-resistant, hot-tire proof, 10-year warranty. Call 503-501-7295.
flake-floors.h1: Full-Broadcast Flake Epoxy Floors in Portland, OR
flake-floors.sub: The toughest, best-looking garage floor you can buy — installed in a single day.
body_paragraphs: Flake floors are our most-requested residential system, and for good reason. We diamond-grind your slab down to clean, open concrete, roll a 100%-solids epoxy basecoat, and broadcast colored vinyl flake to rejection — meaning we keep throwing chips until the floor literally can't hold any more. That dense flake layer is what gives the finished floor its texture, its slip resistance, and its signature look. Once the basecoat cures, we scrape the floor flat, vacuum the excess, and seal everything under two coats of UV-stable polyaspartic. The result is a seamless, sanitary, showroom-grade surface that laughs off hot tires, dropped wrenches, jack stands, and Oregon road salt.

Flake is the right call for almost any Portland garage. It hides dust, road grit, and the occasional oil drip. The texture gives you real traction when you walk in from a rainy driveway. And because we install the entire system in a single day, you drop your cars off in the morning and park them back inside that night — no week-long displacement, no sleeping with the garage door cracked. We stock over a dozen standard flake blends (from classic domino to custom PNW earth tones) and can match almost any palette you bring us.

Every flake floor we install includes full moisture mitigation on the slab edges, a cove-base option where the floor meets the wall, and a written 10-year warranty. We don't cut corners on prep, we don't use box-store kits, and we don't disappear after the check clears. If you want a garage floor that still looks new in 2036, this is the system.
features: 100%-solids epoxy basecoat with full-broadcast vinyl flake
Diamond-ground prep — no acid etching, ever
Slip-resistant texture rated for wet garage entries
ideal_for: Shop floors and home hobby spaces

faq.q: How long does a flake floor last?
faq.a: Installed properly over a diamond-ground slab, a flake system will last 20-plus years in a residential garage. Our warranty covers the first ten, but the floor itself is built to outlive the warranty by a wide margin.

faq.q: Can you do it in one day?
faq.a: Yes. We grind, coat, broadcast, scrape, and topcoat in a single day. You can walk on it that evening and park a vehicle on it within 24 hours.

metallic-epoxy.title: Metallic Epoxy Floors
metallic-epoxy.meta_description: Custom metallic epoxy floors for Portland homes and showrooms. 3D depth, mirror gloss, 10-year warranty. Free quote at 503-501-7295.
metallic-epoxy.h1: Metallic Epoxy Floors in Portland & Beaverton
metallic-epoxy.sub: Showroom-grade 3D floors that look like polished stone, liquid metal, or flowing water.
body_paragraphs: Metallic epoxy is a statement floor. We blend reflective mica pigments into a clear 100%-solids epoxy, pour it onto your prepared slab, and hand-work the material with solvent, torches, and rollers to create swirls, lenses, and three-dimensional depth that no two floors ever share. Every metallic we install is one of a kind. Homeowners in the West Hills use it in wine cellars and basement bars. Beaverton dealerships use it on showroom floors. Tigard med-spas use it in lobbies. Anywhere the floor is part of the experience, metallic earns its keep.

The system is more than eye candy. Underneath the artistic topcoat is a full epoxy build — diamond-ground concrete, a pigmented basecoat, the metallic pour, and two coats of high-gloss polyaspartic on top. That stack is fully waterproof, chemically resistant, easy to mop, and rated for showroom and light commercial traffic. It handles dropped glassware, spilled wine, and a decade of foot traffic without yellowing, chalking, or losing its mirror gloss. Because polyaspartic is UV-stable, the floor holds its color even under big south-facing windows — a real concern in Portland homes with modern glass walls.

Metallic is a craft install. We spend time with you picking pigments, mocking up sample boards, and walking through the space so the finished floor matches the light, the cabinetry, and the vibe you're after. Lead times run slightly longer than a flake install because of the sample process, but the floor itself still goes in over a single working day. Pricing varies with color count and square footage — call us for a quick in-home quote.
features: Custom-blended metallic pigments, sampled to your space
ideal_for: Basement bars, wine cellars, and home theaters

faq.q: Will the gloss dull over time?
faq.a: Not for a long time. Our polyaspartic topcoat is engineered for showroom use and holds its gloss for 10-plus years under normal interior traffic. A simple mop-up is all the maintenance most floors ever need.

faq.q: Can I pick the colors?
faq.a: Absolutely. We carry dozens of mica pigments and will build sample boards in your home or shop before we install. You sign off on the exact palette before we pour a drop.

quartz-floors.title: Quartz Epoxy Floors
quartz-floors.meta_description: Double-broadcast quartz floors for Portland restaurants, kitchens, and wet rooms. USDA-grade, slip-resistant, sanitary. Call 503-501-7295.
quartz-floors.h1: Quartz Epoxy Floors in the Portland Metro
quartz-floors.sub: USDA-friendly, slip-resistant, sanitary floors built for kitchens, locker rooms, and wet-process spaces.
body_paragraphs: Quartz systems are the workhorse of commercial flooring. We install a double-broadcast of colored quartz aggregate into two separate epoxy basecoats, then seal the stack under a chemical-resistant urethane or polyaspartic topcoat. The finished floor is thick — typically 3/16-inch built up — completely seamless, and extremely slip-resistant even when wet. That combination is why you'll find our quartz installs in commercial kitchens from Beaverton to Gresham, craft breweries in inner Southeast Portland, dog daycares in Tualatin, and lab spaces along the Hillsboro tech corridor.

The advantage of quartz over flake in a commercial setting comes down to thickness, aggregate hardness, and cleanability. Colored quartz is a mined mineral with a Mohs hardness of 7 — harder than most things that will ever roll across it. The double broadcast builds up a dense, puncture-resistant wear layer that shrugs off dropped tools, pallet corners, and heavy rolling loads. And because the entire system is monolithic and cove-able up the wall, there are no grout lines, no seams, and nowhere for bacteria, grease, or standing water to hide. Health inspectors love it. So do the people who have to mop at 2 a.m.

We install quartz in both standard colors and custom blends. For wet kitchens we recommend a textured urethane topcoat that holds an R10-plus slip rating even under grease. For clean rooms and lab spaces we run a smoother polyaspartic that still cleans aggressively but doesn't grab debris. Either way, we finish in phases so your business can keep operating, and we back the install with a 5-year commercial warranty.
features: Seamless monolithic install with integral cove base
ideal_for: Locker rooms, showers, and wet-process rooms

faq.q: Is quartz slippery when wet?
faq.a: No. The broadcast aggregate creates built-in texture that stays grippy even under grease and water. We can dial the aggressiveness up or down depending on your space — kitchen floors get more bite, lab floors get less.

faq.q: How long do I need to close?
faq.a: Most quartz installs take two to three working days. We can work overnight or phase the install room-by-room so you stay open during business hours.

concrete-coatings.title: Concrete Coatings Portland
concrete-coatings.meta_description: Polyaspartic concrete coatings for Portland garages, patios, and shops. One-day install, UV-stable, 10-year warranty. Call 503-501-7295.
concrete-coatings.h1: Polyaspartic Concrete Coatings in Portland, OR
concrete-coatings.sub: Faster cure, UV-stable, and four times stronger than standard epoxy — the modern way to coat concrete.
body_paragraphs: Concrete coating is a catch-all phrase for any high-performance system that seals and protects a slab. At Diamond Group we specialize in polyaspartic coatings — a next-generation chemistry that cures faster than epoxy, resists UV yellowing, and comes out roughly four times stronger in abrasion tests. That combination is why we use polyaspartic as the topcoat on nearly every floor we install, and why we recommend it as a standalone system for covered patios, sunrooms, back porches, and any other slab that sees direct sunlight.

A typical concrete coating project starts with a full diamond grind. We open the pores of the slab with industrial grinders and HEPA-filtered vacuums — no dust plume in your house, no acid wash running down the driveway. We chase every crack and spall with a polyurea repair compound, re-grind the patches flat, and prime the whole slab. From there we either broadcast flake, pour a solid color, or run a neat two-coat polyaspartic depending on the look you want. Because polyaspartic recoats in about two hours, the entire system finishes in a single working day and is ready for foot traffic that evening.

Polyaspartic outperforms old-school epoxy in almost every way that matters in Oregon. It won't yellow under the long summer sun. It stays flexible through winter freeze-thaw cycles. It shrugs off road salt, de-icer, gasoline, and brake fluid. And because it bonds chemically to the primed slab, it won't peel, bubble, or delaminate the way DIY kits from the big-box stores always eventually do. If you've been burned by a cheap coating in the past, this is the fix.
features: 4x the abrasion resistance of standard epoxy
Full diamond-grind prep with HEPA vacuum

faq.q: How is this different from epoxy?
faq.a: Epoxy is an older chemistry that cures slowly and yellows under UV. Polyaspartic cures in hours, stays color-stable in sunlight, and tests about four times stronger in abrasion. It costs a little more per gallon but lasts significantly longer.

faq.q: Will it peel?
faq.a: Not when it's installed correctly. Peeling happens when a coating is applied over a dirty or acid-etched slab. We diamond-grind every floor to clean, porous concrete — which is the only prep method that guarantees a permanent mechanical bond.

grind-seal.title: Grind and Seal Concrete Floors
grind-seal.meta_description: Grind-and-seal concrete floors for Portland warehouses, garages, and retail. Budget-friendly, durable, fast install. Call 503-501-7295.
grind-seal.sub: The industrial-look, budget-smart option — your existing slab, ground smooth and sealed for decades.
body_paragraphs: Grind-and-seal is the most cost-effective way to turn a rough, dusty, or stained concrete slab into a clean, durable, easy-to-maintain floor. We run a multi-pass diamond grind to flatten the surface, open the capillaries, and expose the natural aggregate in the slab. Then we seal the whole floor with a two-coat densifier and topcoat system — either a low-sheen urethane for a matte industrial look or a higher-build polyaspartic for a semi-gloss finish. The existing concrete becomes the finished floor. No flake, no color, no resurfacing — just your slab, made permanent.

This system makes sense when the concrete is already in decent shape and the owner wants durability without the price tag of a full resinous buildup. We install it in Vancouver distribution warehouses, Sherwood machine shops, Portland loft conversions, and showroom spaces where the raw-concrete aesthetic is the point. It's also our go-to recommendation for garages where the homeowner wants dust control and stain resistance but doesn't care about color or pattern. Monthly maintenance is a dust mop and the occasional wet mop — that's it.

Where grind-and-seal shines is lifespan per dollar. Because there's no resinous wear layer to wear through, the topcoat can be refreshed every 5 to 7 years for a fraction of the original install cost, extending the life of the floor almost indefinitely. We densify the slab with a lithium silicate hardener during prep, which chemically strengthens the top quarter-inch of concrete and reduces future cracking. Combined with a high-solids topcoat, it's an incredibly low-maintenance floor.
features: Multi-pass diamond grind with HEPA vacuum
Lithium silicate densifier for long-term hardness
Choice of matte urethane or semi-gloss polyaspartic sealer
ideal_for: Garages where an industrial look is wanted

faq.q: Will it hide cracks?
faq.a: Hairline cracks get filled and ground flat, but grind-and-seal isn't meant to hide major damage — it celebrates the existing slab. If your concrete has serious issues we'll recommend a resinous buildup instead and tell you straight up during the quote.

faq.q: Can it be done on old stained concrete?
faq.a: Usually yes. Diamond grinding removes years of oil, paint, and surface staining. In cases of deep oil saturation we pre-treat with an industrial degreaser, but most slabs clean up beautifully.

solid-color.title: Solid Color Epoxy Floors
solid-color.meta_description: Solid color epoxy floors for Portland garages and shops. Clean, simple, durable. One-day install with 10-year warranty. Call 503-501-7295.
solid-color.h1: Solid Color Epoxy Floors in Portland & Beaverton
solid-color.sub: Clean lines, uniform color, industrial-grade durability — the classic garage and shop floor, done right.
body_paragraphs: Sometimes you don't want flake, you don't want metallic swirls, and you don't want the raw concrete look. You want a clean, uniform, solid-color floor — battleship gray, tile red, safety yellow, or a custom-matched shade that ties into your cabinets or brand palette. We install solid-color systems in exactly the same way we install our premium flake floors: full diamond grind, 100%-solids pigmented epoxy basecoat, and a two-coat polyaspartic topcoat. The only difference is what goes in the middle.

Solid-color epoxy is the right call for several specific use cases. It's the traditional finish for industrial and commercial shop floors where line striping matters and high contrast helps with safety. It's popular in home gyms where a consistent color backdrop makes the space feel more like a professional facility. And it's increasingly requested in modern-build Portland garages where homeowners want the minimalist look of a continuous monochrome floor instead of a textured flake pattern. We can mix to any standard color code — OSHA safety colors, Pantone, Sherwin-Williams, whatever you need.

Durability is identical to our flake system. The finished floor is fully waterproof, chemical-resistant, hot-tire proof, and backed by the same 10-year residential or 5-year commercial warranty. The one tradeoff to know: solid colors show dust and scratches slightly more than flake does, because there's no pattern to break up the eye. For high-traffic homes we recommend a satin or matte polyaspartic finish — it hides normal wear without sacrificing performance. For showrooms and shops we go high-gloss. Either way, the floor goes in during a single working day.
features: Available in gloss, satin, or matte finish

faq.q: Will the color fade in sunlight?
faq.a: No. Our polyaspartic topcoat is UV-stable, which keeps the pigment below from breaking down even under direct sun. Solid colors hold their hue for the full life of the floor — a real concern with cheaper epoxy-only systems that tend to yellow and fade.

faq.q: Can you match a specific brand color?
faq.a: Yes. Bring us a swatch, a paint code, or even a product sample and we'll color-match the pigment. We routinely match Sherwin-Williams, Benjamin Moore, and brand-specific safety colors for commercial clients.

commercial-industrial.title: Commercial & Industrial Epoxy Floors
commercial-industrial.meta_description: Heavy-duty epoxy floors for Portland warehouses, shops, breweries, and manufacturing. Phased installs, 5-year warranty. Call 503-501-7295.
commercial-industrial.h1: Commercial & Industrial Epoxy Floors in Portland
commercial-industrial.sub: Heavy-duty resinous systems engineered for warehouses, breweries, manufacturing, and distribution.
body_paragraphs: Commercial and industrial flooring isn't a bigger version of a residential garage job — it's a different discipline. We've spent years installing resinous systems in warehouses, production lines, breweries, auto shops, distribution centers, and light-manufacturing spaces across the Portland metro and Southwest Washington. Every commercial project starts with a site walk, a moisture test, a service-load discussion, and a written spec that ties the right system to the right use case. A brewery needs thermal-shock-rated urethane. A forklift-heavy warehouse needs a thick quartz buildup. A machine shop needs chemical resistance. We won't sell you a floor that's wrong for the job, and we won't undersell one that won't survive.

Operationally, we install around your schedule, not ours. We run weekend crews, overnight shifts, and phased room-by-room installs so production never fully stops. We set up HEPA-filtered negative-pressure containment so dust doesn't migrate into clean areas or adjacent tenants. We coordinate with facility managers, GCs, and food-safety auditors. And every commercial install is documented with thickness measurements, slab moisture readings, batch records of every material applied, and a final walk-through punch list signed by your operations lead. That documentation matters at audit time.

Systems we install commercially include full quartz broadcast, double-broadcast flake, metallic showroom floors, solid-color industrial coatings, cement urethane, trench-drain integration, and slip-rated textured topcoats. We carry $2M in liability coverage, full workers comp, and every certification required to work in food-service and regulated environments. References on request — we'd rather have you call three of our past commercial clients than read another webpage of marketing copy.
features: Full-service resinous systems (quartz, flake, metallic, cement urethane)
Phased and after-hours installs to protect production
Thickness and moisture documentation for audits

faq.q: Can you install while we stay open?
faq.a: Almost always. We run overnight and weekend crews, phase the install room-by-room, and use fast-curing polyaspartic or cement urethane systems that let you walk on the new floor within hours. We'll build a schedule around your production calendar.

faq.q: Do you handle the disposal and environmental side?
faq.a: Yes. We capture grind dust with HEPA-filtered vacuums, contain any surface contaminants, and dispose of waste through licensed channels. For regulated facilities we provide full material data sheets and install documentation for your records.

faq.q: How long does an epoxy floor take to install?
faq.a: Most residential garage floors are finished in a single working day. We arrive early, diamond-grind the slab, apply the basecoat and any flake or metallic layer, and finish with a polyaspartic topcoat by late afternoon. You can walk on the floor that evening and park a vehicle on it within 24 hours.

faq.q: Do you use epoxy or polyaspartic?
faq.a: Both — as a system. We use a 100%-solids epoxy basecoat for its bond strength, then finish with a two-coat polyaspartic topcoat for UV stability, chemical resistance, and abrasion performance. The combination outlasts either chemistry used alone, which is why it's our standard system on every residential floor.

faq.q: Will hot tires damage the floor?
faq.a: No. Our polyaspartic topcoat is specifically engineered to resist hot-tire pickup, which is the single most common failure point on cheap garage floors. You can pull a car straight off the freeway into a hot garage and park on our coating without leaving a mark.

faq.q: Do you grind or acid-etch the concrete?
faq.a: We diamond-grind every floor. Acid etching was a shortcut popular with DIY kits and low-end contractors, and it simply does not create a reliable bond on Oregon concrete. Diamond grinding opens the capillaries mechanically, removes surface contaminants, and guarantees the coating adheres for the life of the slab.

faq.q: What's your warranty?
faq.a: Every residential floor we install comes with a 10-year written warranty covering delamination, peeling, and hot-tire pickup. Commercial floors carry a 5-year written warranty. We've been installing long enough to stand behind our work — the warranty is there because we believe in it, not because we expect to use it.

faq.q: Can you install over cracked or oil-stained concrete?
faq.a: Almost always, yes. Diamond grinding removes years of oil and surface damage, and we fill cracks with a polyurea repair compound that's stronger than the surrounding concrete. In extreme cases we may recommend partial slab work, but we're straight with you during the quote — no surprises.

faq.q: How much does an epoxy floor cost?
faq.a: Most residential garages run between $6 and $11 per square foot depending on size, system, and condition of the existing slab. A typical two-car garage lands around $3,500 to $5,000 installed. We quote every project in person and our written estimates are good for 30 days.

faq.q: Do I need to move everything out of the garage?
faq.a: Yes, the garage needs to be empty on install day so we can grind the entire slab corner to corner. We're happy to coordinate scheduling around your move-out, and we've had clients rent a PODS container for a day or two. Once the floor cures overnight, you can move everything back in.

faq.q: Will the floor be slippery when wet?
faq.a: No. The flake in our standard system creates enough surface texture to stay grippy even when water is tracked in from a rainy driveway. For extra-slippery-prone environments — commercial kitchens, wet rooms — we can add aluminum-oxide grit to increase traction further.

faq.q: Are you licensed and insured?
faq.a: Yes. We carry full Oregon CCB licensing, $2M in general liability coverage, and workers comp on every crew member. Our WA license covers work across the river. Certificates of insurance are available on request before any commercial project.
